faqs.question: What does Sputum by Conventional Method measure?
faqs.answer: This test analyses the sputum sample to identify abnormal cells, bacteria, fungi, and other substances.

faqs.question: Why is Sputum by Conventional Method done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose respiratory infections and diseases such as tuberculosis, pneumonia, or bronchitis • To detect lung cancer or other tumours • To monitor ongoing treatment effectiveness for lung conditions • To assess the presence of abnormal cells or organisms in the lungs • To guide appropriate treatment decisions based on the findings

faqs.question: When is Sputum by Conventional Method recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may recommend this test if you have • Persistent cough with or without sputum production. • Symptoms such as chest pain, difficulty breathing, or unexplained weight loss. • Suspected respiratory infections or tuberculosis. • A family history of lung cancer or other lung diseases. • Been exposed to certain risk factors like smoking or occupational hazards.

faqs.question: What if the results of Sputum by Conventional Method are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results might indicate • Infections such as bacterial pneumonia or tuberculosis. • Presence of abnormal cells suggesting lung cancer or pre-cancerous conditions. • Inflammatory conditions like bronchitis or asthma. Further evaluation and diagnostic tests will be needed to confirm the underlying cause and guide appropriate treatment.

faqs.question: What to expect during Sputum by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: During this test: • You will be given a container to collect a sputum sample. • You will be asked to cough deeply and spit the sputum into the container. • The sample should be collected in the morning before eating or drinking anything. • The sample will then be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before Sputum by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: To prepare for this test: • Rinse your mouth with water before collecting the sputum sample to avoid contamination. • Try to produce a deep cough to bring up enough sputum. • Avoid eating, drinking, or brushing your teeth for at least one hour before collecting the sample. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with Sputum by Conventional Method?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be recommended along with Sputum by Conventional Method include: • Chest X-ray or CT scan: To assess the structure and condition of the lungs. • Pulmonary Function Test: To evaluate lung function and capacity. • Bronchoscopy: To visualise the airways and collect samples directly from the lungs.

faqs.question: What is Sputum by Conventional Method also known as?
What is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)?
faqs.answer: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a progressive lung disease characterized by airflow limitation and breathing difficulties. It includes conditions such as chronic bronchitis and emphysema. COPD is often diagnosed through tests like spirometry and sputum analysis.
